newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister orders probe into Islamist firebrand.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister orders probe into Islamist firebrand.

text.p: A Turkish minister in the Islamist wing of the coalition government on Friday ordered a legal probe into one of his own MPs for a speech he made seven years ago attacking Turkey's secular system, media and the parliament.
"I ordered the Ankara chief prosecutor to investigate Sevki Yilmaz's speech that was broadcast by some television channels," Anatolian news agency quoted Justice Minister Sevket Kazan as saying.
Yilmaz, a deputy from the ruling Islamist Welfare Party, said in a speech to followers made in 1990 that enforcing Turkey's strict secularism was equal to imposing Christianity on Moslem Turkey.
His comments were broadcast on Turkish television for the first time on Thursday night.

"The Turkish state has a religion and that is Christianity," said Yilmaz, known as an Islamist firebrand. "The Turkish penal code and the Turkish civil law are formed in line with the Bible," he said. He also described parliamentarians as "pimps" for making these laws.
A senior member of the Welfare's coalition partner True Path Party called for Yilmaz, who has parliamentary immunity from prosecution, to quit.
"If he actually has said these words, he should not stay in the parliament, he should leave," Anatolian quoted True Path deputy Hayri Kozakcioglu as saying.

Relations between ruling Islamists and the country's secularist establishment have been strained since a military-dominated council ordered Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to curb rising religious activism in February.
The army pressure has brought the coalition close to breaking point.
